title: Base changes of a smooth curve are smooth of relative dimension $1$
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $C$ be a curve over $k$ [def-pc-curve] (an integral scheme, separated and of finite type over $k$, of dimension $1$) whose structure morphism $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $T$ be a scheme with a morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $C_T=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}T$ be the base change [def-pc-base-change] and $f_T:C_T\to T$ the second projection. Then $f_T$ is smooth of relative dimension $1$ in the sense of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: $f_T$ is smooth, and for every point $x\in C_T$, with $t=f_T(x)$ and fibre $(C_T)_t=C_T\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$, the dimension of $(C_T)_t$ at $x$ [def-kun-dimension] is $\dim_x\bigl((C_T)_t\bigr)=1$.

proof.text: The structure morphism C\to\operatorname{Spec}k is smooth by hypothesis. The projection f_T:C_T\to T is its base change along T\to\operatorname{Spec}k, so f_T is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2), the base-change stability of smooth morphisms in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms].

source.place: Tag 01VB (lemma-base-change-smooth), equivalently Tags 02H2 and 01TS for the formal-smooth definition

proof.text: For x\in C_T with t=f_T(x), the fibre (C_T)_t is canonically C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t) by associativity of the fibre-product defining C_T and the scheme-theoretic fibre. Thus it is the fibre of C\to\operatorname{Spec}k after base change to \kappa(t), and x maps to a point of C.

Apply [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] to C\to\operatorname{Spec}k and T\to\operatorname{Spec}k. The fibre of C\to\operatorname{Spec}k over its unique point s is C itself, since \kappa(s)=k, so the X_s occurring in that lemma is C. It gives dim_x((C_T)_t)=dim_y(C), where y is the image of x in C. By [def-pc-curve], dim C=1 in the sense of [def-pc-dimension]. Hence the topological dimension of C is 1 by [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], and dim_y(C)=1 for every y by [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic], because C is integral and therefore irreducible and its structure morphism is of finite type, hence locally of finite type. Thus dim_x((C_T)_t)=1 for every x.
